## Table S1. Per-Fold Cross-Validation Setup

The v33 benchmark stores pooled out-of-fold (OOF) AUROC, 95% bootstrap CI, and AUPRC per method–cohort pair (`results/benchmark/v33/benchmark_v33.json`). Per-fold AUROC values are fully determined by the archived split files (SHA1 recorded in `results/run_registry.json`) and are reproducible with `scripts/rerun_v33.py`. The fold structure per cohort:

| Cohort–endpoint | n | k (folds) | Endpoint note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hugo 2016 RECIST (n=28) | 28 | 5 | RECIST v1.1, 13 responders |
| Lauss 2017 (ACT) RECIST (n=25) | 25 | 5 | RECIST v1.1, 10 responders |
| Gide 2019 RECIST (n=73) | 73 | 5 | RECIST v1.1, 40 responders |
| Jung 2019 DCB (n=27) | 27 | 5 | DCB, 6 responders (labels corrected v33: 1 = DCB) |
| Riaz 2017 cytolytic (n=43) | 43 | 5 | cytolytic above median, 21/43 |
| Riaz 2017 RECIST (n=42) | 42 | 2 | RECIST v1.1, 9 responders → k = 2 (primary); k = 2/3/5 in Table S16 |

## Table S2. Literature Comparison: Published vs. SPATBench Standardized AUROC (v33)

| Method | Published AUROC | Published Cohort | SPATBench best (v33) | Inflation | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TIDE | 0.80 | IMvigor210 (BLCA, n = 298) | 0.752 (Gide 2019 RECIST) | +0.05 | Jiang et al. 2018, Nature Medicine |
| IMPRES | 0.83 | Auslander 2018 (SKCM, n = 30–48) | 0.795 (Hugo 2016 RECIST) | +0.04 | Auslander et al. 2018, Nature Medicine |
| TMB (proxy) | 0.64 | Various (n > 100) | 0.500 constant proxy | +0.14 | Goodman et al. 2017, Mol Cancer Ther |
| PD-L1 (CD274) | 0.65 | Multiple trials | 0.868 (Riaz 2017 cytolytic) | -0.22 | Topalian et al. 2012, NEJM |
| GEP | 0.67 | IMvigor210 (BLCA, n = 298) | 0.968 (Riaz 2017 cytolytic) | -0.30 | Mariathasan et al. 2018, Nature |
| ElasticNet (MI) | 0.80 | Multiple (n > 200) | 0.968 (Riaz 2017 cytolytic) | -0.17 | Chowell et al. 2022, Nature Biotechnology |

*SPATBench best values are the maximum AUROC across the six v33 cohort–endpoints (leakage-free nested CV); the TMB proxy is a constant 0.5 baseline (real mutation data unavailable) and the PD-L1 proxy is CD274 expression (real IHC scores unavailable).*

**Caveat:** Published values come from different (typically larger) cohorts. This comparison illustrates cross-study variability, not a within-cohort evaluation. Inflation (published minus SPATBench best) ranges from -0.30 to +0.14.

## Table S4. Circularity Detection Score (CDS)

### (a) Values as reported in manuscript Table 3 (archived computation)

| Endpoint | CDS | C1 (MI) | C2 (ρ) | Risk (recalibrated, HIGH > 0.80) | Inflated? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riaz 2017 cytolytic | 0.954 | 0.573 | 0.845 | HIGH | **Yes** |
| Lauss 2017 (ACT) RECIST | 0.781 | 0.049 | 0.294 | MODERATE | No |
| Riaz 2017 RECIST | 0.685 | 0.034 | 0.273 | MODERATE | No |
| Hugo 2016 RECIST | 0.449 | <0.001 | 0.164 | MODERATE | No |

*Archived-provenance note: the two Riaz values were computed on the pre-v33 Entrez-ID matrices (endpoint genes recorded as Entrez 3001/5551); all other cohorts use HGNC symbol matrices. The recalibrated risk labels use the conservative HIGH > 0.80 boundary (candidate for CDS v2.0); under the shipped v1.1.0 threshold (HIGH > 0.70) Lauss (0.781) is labelled HIGH by the released tool.*

### (b) v33 recomputation with cds v1.1.0 on the HGNC matrices (uniform convention; scripts/supplementary_v33_experiments.py)

All five evaluable endpoints, declared endpoint genes GZMA/PRF1, cds v1.1.0 (weights 30/30/40, shipped thresholds HIGH > 0.70, MODERATE 0.30–0.70), each with its cohort-matched random-label null (10 replicates, `cds_nulls_v33.json`; the manuscript Table 3 now reports the upgraded 200-replicate nulls from `cds_nulls_200_v33.json` — all Table 3 readings are unchanged under the 200-replicate nulls):

| Endpoint (v33 matrix) | CDS | C1 (MI) | C2 (ρ) | C3 | null mean | null max | CDS vs null | Risk (shipped v1.1.0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hugo 2016 RECIST | 0.449 | 0.000 | 0.164 | 1.000 | 0.608 | 0.764 | at/below null mean | MODERATE |
| Lauss 2017 (ACT) RECIST | 0.781 | 0.049 | 0.294 | 1.000 | 0.557 | 0.832 | above null mean | HIGH |
| Gide 2019 RECIST | 0.852 | 0.141 | 0.508 | 1.000 | 0.518 | 0.726 | far above null max | HIGH |
| Riaz 2017 RECIST (v33) | 0.409 | 0.000 | 0.029 | 1.000 | 0.556 | 0.742 | at/below null mean | MODERATE |
| Riaz 2017 cytolytic | 0.954 | 0.573 | 0.845 | 1.000 | 0.510 | 0.764 | far above null max | HIGH |

**Recomputation notes (disclosed, not silently reconciled):**

1. Hugo (0.449), Lauss (0.781) and Riaz cytolytic (0.954) reproduce the archived scores exactly. Riaz RECIST recomputes to **0.409** on the HGNC matrix versus the archived 0.685 (Entrez space) — the archived value should be read as Entrez-space; the HGNC-space value is the one consistent with the v33 benchmark feature space.
2. **Gide 2019 RECIST has a stored CDS value for the first time: 0.852 (HIGH under both the shipped 0.70 and the conservative 0.80 boundary).** The manuscript narrative that CDS predicted Gide 'LOW' is not supported by this recomputation. Mechanistically, C1 and C2 read the strong association between the declared genes (GZMA/PRF1) and the clinical RECIST label in this large melanoma cohort — the same association that underlies the genuine GEP result (0.830, q < 0.001) — as endpoint-gene dependency. This is the CDS limitation discussed in the manuscript (inability to separate genuine immune-biology signal from circularity) made concrete; the CDS risk vocabulary should be read as advisory (Methods), and the Gide CDS value is reported here for transparency pending the CDS v2.0 redesign.
3. Risk labels in (a) use the recalibrated HIGH > 0.80 boundary; the tool's shipped labels (column 'Risk (shipped v1.1.0)' above) flag Lauss and Gide as HIGH. The validated claim therefore needs the 0.80 boundary and, for Gide, does not hold under any current threshold — see note 2.

### (c) Synthetic null distribution (30 random-label replicates, quoted from Methods)

Mean null CDS = 0.50 (SD = 0.09), 95th percentile = 0.65, 99th percentile = 0.71; ≈3% of random endpoints flagged HIGH under the shipped threshold due to C3 saturation at 1.0. The 30 null replicates were generated after the real endpoints had been inspected (retrospective calibration; Methods).

### (d) Synthetic five-scenario ranking (cds_synthetic_calibration_v3.json)

| Scenario | Circularity level | CDS | Mean AUROC | Risk (shipped) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pure random endpoint | 0.697 | 0.468 | MODERATE |
| 2 | ~20% circular, 80% biological | 0.820 | 0.691 | HIGH |
| 3 | ~50% circular, 50% biological | 0.830 | 0.838 | HIGH |
| 4 | ~80% circular, 20% biological | 0.832 | 0.788 | HIGH |
| 5 | 100% circular endpoint | 0.845 | 0.845 | HIGH |

CDS ranks all five scenarios monotonically (0.697 < 0.820 < 0.830 < 0.832 < 0.845). Endpoints with CDS ≥ 0.80 show inflated AUROC (0.691–0.845); the pure-random scenario sits at CDS 0.697 — above the manuscript's earlier '0.51' description, which came from the alternative v2 calibration (endpoint-weight parameterization, `cds_synthetic_calibration_v2.json`, scenario 1: CDS 0.513). The two calibrations parameterize circularity differently and are not interchangeable.

**Threshold disclosure:** one threshold set is shipped everywhere (HIGH > 0.70, MODERATE 0.30–0.70, LOW ≤ 0.30); the conservative 0.80 boundary (0/30 false positives on the synthetic null) is the candidate for CDS v2.0. Continuous CDS values should be reported; categorical labels are advisory.

## Table S5. Method Concordance — Cohen's κ (Hugo 2016, n = 28, v33)

OOF predictions under the v33 leakage-free protocol (ElasticNet-MI frozen at C = 1.0, l1_ratio = 0.1); each method's continuous score binarized at its own median. All 10 method pairs are reported.

| Method pair | Agreement | Cohen's κ |
|---|---|---|
| IMPRES vs. GEP | 57% | 0.143 |
| IMPRES vs. TIDE | 50% | 0.000 |
| IMPRES vs. PD-L1 (CD274 expr.) | 71% | 0.429 |
| IMPRES vs. ElasticNet (MI) | 57% | 0.143 |
| GEP vs. TIDE | 50% | 0.000 |
| GEP vs. PD-L1 (CD274 expr.) | 79% | 0.571 |
| GEP vs. ElasticNet (MI) | 57% | 0.143 |
| TIDE vs. PD-L1 (CD274 expr.) | 50% | 0.000 |
| TIDE vs. ElasticNet (MI) | 64% | 0.286 |
| PD-L1 (CD274 expr.) vs. ElasticNet (MI) | 57% | 0.143 |

8 of 10 pairs fall below the conventional fair-agreement threshold (κ = 0.40); the highest is GEP vs. PD-L1 (CD274 expr.) (κ = 0.571) — the concordance of two fixed scorers, not a trained model; the highest pair involving the trainable method is TIDE vs. ElasticNet (MI) (κ = 0.286). At n = 28 different methods flag largely different patients as responders.

*The ranking advantage of the cohort's only FDR-significant method (AUROC 0.795) does not translate into decision utility: at the 0.5 threshold it labels 92% of patients responders, its net benefit coincides with treat-all at 10–20% thresholds, and its reclassification metrics do not exceed the random baseline. The IMPRES score is an uncalibrated fraction, so these metrics reflect threshold behavior rather than calibrated risk; the same reading follows either way — a high AUROC alone does not establish clinical usefulness.*

## Table S11. Complete Permutation Test Matrix (v33)

Fixed scorers (IMPRES, GEP, TIDE, PD-L1): 50,000 label shuffles against the fixed score (mathematically equivalent to the full-pipeline null because the score is label-independent; the equivalence was verified on Hugo IMPRES). Trainable methods (ElasticNet-MI, ElasticNet-Var): full-pipeline label shuffles with frozen hyperparameters, per-cell n. BH correction within each cohort.

| Method | Cohort | n | Obs AUROC | Perm-obs AUROC | p | n (shuffles) | BH q | Significant |

*Trainable-method p-values are computed against the frozen-hyperparameter Perm-obs AUROC (right column), not the tuned benchmark Obs AUROC; see the footnote below.*

The Obs AUROC column shows the benchmark AUROC (tune-primary protocol). The Perm-obs AUROC column shows the observed AUROC under the permutation protocol. For the trainable cells re-run with frozen hyperparameters (recorded in results/benchmark/v33/nc_cells/*.json, summarized in perm_obs_auroc_v33.json) it deviates from the benchmark value by 0.000–0.103 (largest: Hugo ElasticNet-MI 0.528 vs 0.631 — frozen-versus-tuned hyperparameters, the same deviation class as the Gide ElasticNet-MI cell, which re-run at 5,000 shuffles gives 0.662 vs the benchmark 0.629, i.e. +0.033). On 2026-09-18 all eight clinical trainable cells were extended to a uniform minimum of 2,000 full-pipeline shuffles (four cells at 5,000) as a pre-registered resolution-hardening check (`scripts/extend_nc_cells_5000.py`, merged by `scripts/merge_nc_cells_ext.py`): no cell changed its significance verdict, and the smallest within-cohort trainable q at n ≤ 43 tightened from 0.108 to 0.0716 (Lauss); the merge is reversible via the pre-merge snapshot `permutation_v33.pre_ext_backup.json`. For the remaining four trainable cells (Gide MI/Var and Riaz cytolytic MI/Var) the permutation-run AUROC reproduces the benchmark value within 0.0003. For fixed scorers the observed score is the benchmark AUROC by construction (the score is label-independent); PD-L1 cells use the fixed-scorer protocol (`scripts/pdl1_perm_v33.py`).*


Cells surviving within-cohort BH (q < 0.05): 12. Of these, the trainable-method cells are: ElasticNet (MI) on Gide 2019 RECIST (n=73) (0.629, q = 0.028), ElasticNet (Var) on Gide 2019 RECIST (n=73) (0.605, q = 0.028), ElasticNet (MI) on Riaz 2017 cytolytic (n=43) (0.968, q = 0.003), ElasticNet (Var) on Riaz 2017 cytolytic (n=43) (0.985, q = 0.002). No trainable method survives FDR at n ≤ 43; Gide (n = 73) is the first sample size at which a training-based signature becomes detectable, consistent with the power analysis.

Cohort details: SKCM n = 441 (212 events); BRCA n = 1082 (151 events); LUAD n = 510 (185 events); COAD n = 458 (102 events). The stromal signature is the only non-significant one in SKCM and the only one with HR > 1 (1.086) — an internal negative control. HR < 1 = protective per 1 SD of the z-standardized signature. Univariate models; machine-readable in `data/tcga/tcga_cox_all.json`.

**Sample-type decomposition (SKCM).** The v33 SKCM policy is all-tumour samples, metastatic-dominant, while COAD (GDC) is primary-only — a composition difference the cross-cancer gradient partially conflates with cancer type. A three-arm decomposition of the identical 12-signature Cox + BH pipeline (`scripts/tcga_skcm_sampletype_sensitivity.py`; computed on cBioPortal-API-refetched matrices, the all-tumour arm reproducing the archived 11/12 with HR 0.795–0.928 exactly and thereby validating the refetch): all-tumour n = 434 (212 events), 11/12 BH-significant; **metastatic-only n = 360 (187 events), 11/12 BH-significant (HR 0.789–0.934)**; primary-only n = 76 (27 events), 0/12. The SKCM signal is carried by the metastatic arm and is internally robust to the composition question; the SKCM-versus-COAD sides of the gradient should be read as metastatic-dominant versus primary-only disease.

**Multivariate sensitivity (SKCM).** Cox models adjusted for age and AJCC stage (n = 390, 191 events; signature, age and stage z-standardized; stage parsed from AJCC codes to ordinal 1–4): **8/12 signatures remain BH-significant** with stronger protective HRs (0.569–0.704) than the univariate models — the immune-prognostic signal is not a stage- or age-proxy (`scripts/tcga_skcm_multivariate.py`, `SKCM_cox_multivariate.json`).

**Reading.** All 60 pseudo-endpoints — ECM/stromal, proliferation and lineage programs alike — score above the HIGH boundary, exactly like the cytolytic positive control, while random-label nulls stay lower (though with 3/10 replicates above 0.70 on the n = 28 feature space). CDS therefore measures the gene-definedness of an endpoint, program-agnostically: it detects circular *construction*, cannot grade *content*, and its categorical thresholds carry no specificity among structured endpoints. This quantifies the C3-saturation limitation and motivates the CDS v2.0 redesign.

## Note S1. Synthetic Data Validation

On the bundled synthetic cohort (SYNTH_TEST, n = 200; regenerated during the v33 validation fixes), the framework recovers the planted predictive signal: GEP AUROC = 0.679 on synthetic data with known ground-truth signal
, IMPRES = 0.500
, ElasticNet-MI = 0.623
. The archived v28 note (n = 200, 2,000 genes; GEP 0.726 / EN-MI 0.546) refers to a superseded synthetic generator and is superseded by the current `benchmark_results_VALIDATION.json`.

## Note S2. TIDE Implementation Validation

v33 evaluates TIDE through the official `tidepy` v1.3.9 package directly. On Hugo 2016 RECIST, tidepy returns AUROC = 0.426; on Riaz 2017 (HGNC-mapped) TIDE is near chance on both endpoints (RECIST 0.466, cytolytic 0.470), consistent with the tidepy source check (classification = correlation['TIDE'] < vthres, default vthres = 0). The earlier simplified in-repo TIDE implementation (v28, 0.410 on Hugo) agreed with the official package when compared and has been retired in favor of the official package.

## Note S3. Cohort Acquisition and Quality Control (v33 updates)

Cohorts were downloaded from GEO (GEOquery) or cBioPortal (cBioPortalData; Gide 2019 via mel_iatlas_gide_2019). QC: pre-treatment status confirmation, removal of samples with missing response annotations, gene-level filtering, and gene-identifier format validation. v33 data-layer corrections, disclosed in the manuscript: (i) Riaz 2017 matrices stored var_names as Entrez Gene IDs — every symbol-based signature was degenerate (AUROC exactly 0.500); all Riaz results now come from the Entrez→HGNC-mapped matrices (21,769/22,187 genes mapped; `scripts/map_riaz_to_hgnc.py`); (ii) the Riaz RECIST h5ad was a transposed 42×43 label table and was rebuilt (`scripts/rebuild_riaz_recist.py`, n = 42, 22187 genes); (iii) Jung 2019 release codes 1 = NDB — the inverse of every other cohort; v33 uses 1 = DCB (6/27) after verification against GSE135222; (iv) the TCGA pipeline now validates TCGA barcode format and skips incompatible inputs with an explicit warning (the COAD withdrawal in Table S15).

## Note S4. TCGA Cox Regression — Full Methods (v33)

**Data.** TCGA RNA-seq and clinical survival data. SKCM/BRCA/LUAD use the cBioPortal pan-cancer-atlas RSEM matrices (SKCM: all tumour samples, n = 441, 212 deaths; BRCA n = 1,082; LUAD n = 510). COAD was re-acquired from the GDC current index (STAR counts, GENCODE v36, primary tumours, FPKM; clinical from the GDC demographic API; `scripts/build_coad_gdc.py`) after the original non-TCGA raw files forced the v33 withdrawal: n = 458, 102 deaths. For patients with multiple samples the first tumour sample per patient was retained. Non-numeric `OS_MONTHS` values are coerced to missing and dropped; COAD OS_MONTHS = days / 30.436875 (GDC convention).

**Signatures.** 12 immune signatures (44 unique genes; the signature definitions are those of `scripts/run_tcga_cox.py`, overlapping but not identical to the 14-signature Table S10 set) as mean log2(RSEM + 1) of marker genes; the IMPRES-like signature uses the 12 IMPRES genes as mean expression (the pairwise-ratio logic is not applicable in the Cox pipeline).

**Statistics.** Univariate Cox models (lifelines CoxPHFitter); Wald p-values; **Benjamini–Hochberg correction within each cancer type (12 tests each)** — the archived analysis used nominal p < 0.05 only and is superseded. Results: SKCM 11/12, BRCA 3/12, LUAD 1/12, COAD 0/12 signatures significant at FDR < 0.05 (the restored COAD independently reproduces the archived 0/12 finding).

**Limitations.** Univariate models without clinical covariates; IMPRES-like signature is a mean-expression approximation; no time-dependent AUC is reported under v33 (the archived 0.33–0.60 range was not regenerated). Sample-type composition differs across the compared cancer types (SKCM metastatic-dominant; COAD primary-only); the SKCM decomposition in Table S15 shows the gradient signal is metastatic-carried and internally robust.

## Note S5. IMPRES Canonical Implementation — the 15 Pairwise Relations (v33)

v33 implements IMPRES exactly as the published algorithm: the score is the fraction of the following 15 logical relations (gene A > gene B) fulfilled by the sample, linearly rescaled when features are missing, with no retraining. The relations were decoded from the original authors' released feature set (github.com/noamaus/IMPRES-codes, FEATS.mat) and cross-checked against the 9 pairs named in the paper text (9/9 match). ## Note S6. Negative-Control Stress Test — Design and Interpretation (E2)

**Motivation.** The internal CDS validation used four real endpoints and a synthetic null; the question left open was whether CDS separates 'gene-defined circular construction' from 'any structured biology'. This stress test answers it.

**Design.** Thirty canonical gene programs per cohort in three families: (A) ECM/stroma without EMT-TFs (10 sets: fibrillar collagens, fibroblast activation, ECM remodeling, endothelium, pericyte, proteoglycan matrix, basement membrane, myofibroblastic CAF, lymphatic endothelium, protease stroma); (B) tumour purity/proliferation (10 sets: cell cycle, E2F, MYC targets, DNA replication/repair, spindle checkpoint, translation, glycolysis, OXPHOS, stress response, UPR); (C) lineage/signalling programs (10 sets: melanocytic differentiation, keratinocyte basal, hypoxia, interferon, TNF/NF-kB, antigen presentation, complement, senescence, Wnt targets, MHC-II). Each pseudo-endpoint is the median split of the program-mean expression — the identical construction to the cytolytic surrogate — with the program's own genes declared to CDS. Cohorts: Gide 2019 (n = 73) and Hugo 2016 (n = 28). References: the cytolytic surrogate on the same cohort and a 10-replicate random-label null. Gene lists are in `scripts/cds_negative_controls.py`; per-endpoint CDS/C1/C2/C3 in `cds_negative_controls.json`.

**Result.** 60/60 pseudo-endpoints score HIGH (Gide range 0.792–0.942, mean 0.861; Hugo 0.801–0.946, mean 0.869), indistinguishable in band from the cytolytic positive control (0.955 / 0.923), while the random-label nulls sit lower (Gide mean 0.518, max 0.726; Hugo mean 0.608, max 0.764 — note 3/10 Hugo replicates still exceed the shipped 0.70 boundary at n = 28).

**Interpretation.** Both readings are reported and both are used in the manuscript. (1) *Program-agnostic sensitivity:* CDS correctly flags every operationally gene-defined surrogate, whatever the program — the construction itself, not the biology, is what triggers the score; a median-split gene-program endpoint IS circular by construction, so HIGH is the correct answer for all 60. (2) *No specificity among structured endpoints:* because real programs and the circular surrogate land in the same band, and because random labels on small real cohorts can also cross the boundary, the categorical HIGH label cannot distinguish circularity from genuine gene–label biology (the Gide 2019 RECIST case, Table S4b). The validated use of CDS v1.1.0 is therefore the continuous value read against its cohort-matched null, plus the procedural rule that declaring endpoint-defining genes identifies circular construction. Both motivate the permutation-based C3 in CDS v2.0.

**CDS (declared genes GZMA/PRF1):** RECIST 0.750 (HIGH; null mean 0.488 — inflated by the known C3-saturation artefact of CDS v1.1.0 on clinical endpoints), PFS<6mo 0.630 (MODERATE; null mean 0.542), cytolytic surrogate 0.786 (HIGH; null mean 0.536). **Reading:** RECIST leaves PD-L1 expression as the only fixed scorer surviving label permutation (nominal only: BH q = 0.056 within the four-scorer family), consistent with PD-L1 IHC being the clinically approved biomarker in this indication. On the gene-defined surrogate endpoint every method except TIDE inflates substantially (TIDE, with the least feature overlap, stays at chance). The TIDE implementation's internal Entrez conversion drops 16.6% of genes (same behaviour as all other cohorts).

## Table S28. Fourth-Cancer-Type Replication — IMmotion150 ccRCC, Atezolizumab Arm (McDermott 2018; iAtlas harmonized; E1 executed)

Third executed E1 replication, extending Design Choice 1 to renal cell carcinoma. iAtlas harmonization via the cBioPortal API (TPM profile, 39,113 unique HGNC symbols after mean-aggregation of duplicate symbols; log2(TPM+1)); clinical data from the same study's per-patient endpoint (263/263 patients). Atezolizumab arm n = 174 (monotherapy and atezo-bevacizumab combination arms are not separable in the harmonization and are pooled; the sunitinib arm is excluded). Endpoints: RECIST (RESPONDER field; CR/PR vs SD/PD; n = 165 after dropping 9 patients without response annotation; 48 responders), DCB6mo (PFS >= 6 months AND no progression event = 51/174 — the Jung-2019 durable-benefit convention, primary PFS endpoint; this cohort has an event indicator, unlike GSE274975), PFS<6mo time-only (89/174; GSE274975-comparable sensitivity), cytolytic surrogate (GZMA/PRF1 median split). k = min(5, 48, 117) = 5 stratified folds, seed 42 (splits SHA-1 992a2e91105dd2da). GZMB, TIGIT and CD276 are absent from the harmonized profile; the affected signatures degrade automatically (GEP 7/8 genes, exhaustion panel 5/6, IMPRES pairs excluding CD276). Machine-readable: `e1_immotion150.json`; pipeline `scripts/e1_immotion150_executed.py`; fetch `scripts/fetch_immotion150_expression.py`.

**CDS (declared genes GZMA/PRF1):** RECIST 0.741 (HIGH; null mean 0.492), DCB6mo 0.653 (null mean 0.492), PFS<6mo 0.570 (null mean 0.459), cytolytic surrogate 0.945 (HIGH; null mean 0.516) — the largest circularity flag of the replication series. **Reading:** RECIST preserves two clinically deployed signals (GEP — consistent with the IFN-gamma stratification used in the trial literature — and PD-L1 expression, the trial's own stratification biomarker); the durable-benefit endpoint attenuates GEP without abolishing it (BH q = 0.064, nominal only); the time-only PFS variant collapses every fixed signature while ElasticNet-Var retains 0.659, i.e. trainable models appear able to fit PFS-time correlates that are not ICI-specific — an option the fixed scorers do not have; the gene-defined surrogate endpoint produces substantial inflation (Δ = +0.243 over RECIST for GEP).
